name: collaborative_text_editor
spec: Create a collaborative real-time text editor in Python using only the standard library. The system consists of a server and a TUI client. Multiple clients can connect simultaneously and edit the same document with changes propagated in real time using Operational Transformation for conflict resolution. The client uses curses for rendering with syntax highlighting for Python source files. A single well-defined JSON-over-TCP protocol is used for all communication.
features: A server process accepts client connections on a configurable TCP port specified via --port flag
Clients connect specifying a username via --user flag and a room name via --room flag allowing multiple independent documents
Basic password authentication is required to join a room configured via a server-side JSON config file
The server maintains each room's document and persists it to disk after every confirmed operation
The server implements Operational Transformation to correctly resolve concurrent conflicting insert and delete operations from multiple clients
The client renders a full screen curses TUI showing the document content with line numbers
The document viewport scrolls vertically and horizontally to follow the cursor
Standard cursor movement is supported including arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, and Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right for word jumping
Standard editing operations are supported including character insertion, Backspace, Delete, and Enter for newlines
Local edits are immediately reflected in the client display before server acknowledgement using optimistic updates
Remote edits from other users appear in real time with cursor positions correctly transformed
Each connected user's cursor position is shown as a highlighted column marker with their username displayed above it in a distinct color
A status bar at the bottom shows the filename, connected user count, connection status, and current cursor line and column
A sidebar panel shows all currently connected users in the room and their current cursor line number
Python syntax highlighting is applied when the document filename ends in .py coloring keywords, strings, comments, and numbers using curses color pairs
Ctrl+S sends a save request to the server which flushes the document to disk and confirms
Ctrl+F opens an inline search bar that highlights all matches and cycles through them with Enter and Shift+Enter
Ctrl+H opens a find and replace prompt with per-replacement confirmation
Ctrl+L requests an exclusive edit lock on the document preventing other users from editing until the lock is released with Ctrl+L again
Lock requests are queued server-side and granted in FIFO order with all clients notified of lock status changes
Ctrl+Z sends an undo operation to the server which reverses the last operation from this client

All communication uses newline delimited JSON messages over TCP with the following defined message types: connect, ack, operation, cursor_update, lock_request, lock_grant, lock_release, save_request, save_ack, disconnect, error
The server logs all connections, disconnections, operations, lock events, and errors to a timestamped log file
If a client disconnects and reconnects to the same room it receives the full current document state and resumes normally
The server supports at least 10 simultaneous client connections across all rooms without data corruption
